message.content:
It’s hard to pick a single “best” film from 2020 because opinions vary widely, but several titles stood out critically and popularly:

| Year | Film | Why it mattered |
|------|------|-----------------|
| 2020 | **“Soul”** (Disney‑Pixar) | A heartfelt, Oscar‑winning animated feature that won Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. It resonated with audiences worldwide for its philosophical depth and musical brilliance. |
| 2020 | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** (Netflix) | A courtroom drama that earned praise for its sharp script, strong ensemble cast, and timely political relevance. It received multiple award nominations, including Best Picture at the Oscars. |
| 2020 | **“Tenet”** (Christopher Nolan) | Though polarizing, it was a high‑concept blockbuster that pushed the boundaries of action filmmaking and earned acclaim for its technical achievements. |
| 2020 | **“The Invisible Man”** (Netflix) | A modern take on the classic horror story that was lauded for its suspense, direction, and strong performance by Elisabeth Moss. |

If you’re looking for a consensus among critics, “Soul” and “The Trial of the Chicago 7” frequently appear at the top of year‑end lists and award nominations. If you prefer a more mainstream blockbuster experience, “Tenet” might be your pick. Ultimately, the “best” film depends on what you value—storytelling, innovation, cultural impact, or pure entertainment.
